title: [PD] Pack DCP1→DCP-N PD KV transfers into dest-contiguous RDMA blocks (#35762)
body:
Cyclic DCP ownership made the relayout path emit one RDMA per token. Gather owned MLA rows on prefill first so Mooncake/NIXL can send page-sized or larger blocks. DSPARK is left to a follow-up.

## Motivation

DCP assigns KV ownership round-robin **per token** (`owned_offsets = arange(rank, num_kv_tokens, dcp_size)`), so on a DCP1 -> DCP-N PD transfer the source indices are strided and `group_concurrent_contiguous` cannot merge them: the relayout emits **one RDMA descriptor per token per layer** (`tokens x layers` per chunk). The transfer becomes descriptor-bound rather than bandwidth-bound.

## Modifications

- **Pack cyclic DCP rows:** Added a raw-pointer Triton gather and common packing path that turns strided MLA source rows into contiguous blocks, reducing transfer descriptors from one per owned token per layer to destination-contiguous runs.
- **Reuse a dedicated gather stream:** Each worker pack buffer lazily creates and reuses its CUDA gather stream. The stream waits for default-stream KV writes, and packing completes before the transport reads the buffer.
- **Keep pack memory bounded and reusable:** Allocate and register one buffer per transfer worker, size it from the maximum prefill chunk, and assign each DCP rank a fixed region. TP peers sharing a DCP rank reuse the same packed source.
- **Integrate both transports:** Mooncake sends the packed blocks directly. NIXL submits immutable rank regions asynchronously and relies on the existing chunk barrier before repacking the buffer.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/disaggregation/test_kimi_linear_pd_dcp4.py` on 8xB300: **6 passed**, GSM8K **0.91** (threshold 0.88). Covers token + output-logprob parity against a monolithic TP4 reference at 9 chunk/virtual-page boundary lengths, and a 32k needle-in-a-haystack at depths 0.1/0.5/0.9.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Setup.** 8xB300, `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct`. `main` @ `20621aa14b` vs this PR @ `539b78567f`, on both transfer backends.

- **Topology:** prefill TP4/EP4 `dcp=1` (GPU 0-3) -> decode TP4 `dcp=4` (GPU 4-7). `tokenspeed_mla`, `fp8_e4m3` KV, `--page-size 64`, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.80`.
- **Workload:** OSL 32, 2 warmup requests + cache flush per point, freshly launched servers per condition. TTFT/throughput client-measured by `sglang.benchmark.serving --pd-separated`.
- **Controls:** bytes moved identical per point (26.1 / 136.2 / 513.8 MB at ISL 4k / 32k / 128k); packed path verified active on the PR (`4 x 31.5 MB` pack buffers per prefill TP rank) and absent on `main`.

title: [HiCache] Align chunked CUDA host registrations (#36798)
body:
## Motivation

Large HiCache host pools can exceed the practical size of a single `cudaHostRegister` call. Splitting registration at arbitrary byte offsets is also unsafe for page-first copies because one copied page may span two registered ranges, causing `cudaMemcpyBatchAsync` to fail with `invalid argument`.

## Changes

- Register large host buffers in configurable chunks (`SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_REGISTER_CHUNK_GB`, default 256 GB).
- Round every chunk down to an integer multiple of the pool's logical copy-page size.
- Cover MHA, MLA, DSA, Mamba, DeepSeek V4, K-only MHA, and asymmetric K/V page-first/page-first-direct layouts; keep layer-first behavior unchanged.
- Track every successful `(ptr, size)` registration and unregister all chunks during host-pool teardown.
- Roll back already registered chunks in reverse order when a later `cudaHostRegister` call fails.
- Add CPU unit coverage for boundaries, lifecycle cleanup, failure rollback, and all affected host-pool layouts.

This is extracted from #26691 and is independent of MLA host dedup.

## Validation

- Chunk registration tests: `11 passed` plus 12 subtests.
- Related CPU host-pool and environment tests: `51 passed, 19 skipped` plus 4 subtests.
- DCP/general host-pool logic under a macOS-compatible allocator harness: `23 passed` (one Linux SHM case excluded).
- UMBP allocator fallback tests: `3 passed`.
- Full pre-commit checks passed on all touched files.

Their contributions helped improve the correctness, robustness, performance, and production readiness of the implementation.

title: feat(unified-memory): dense KV views for uniform-row MHA/SWA models (#34602)
body:
> **Note on scope — this PR was split**. It previously contained both the dense-view feature and the
> write-location refactor that builds on it. Reviewing a new layout and a cross-cutting refactor together
> made both harder to judge, so the refactor now lives in separate PRs that stack on this one. This PR
> is now purely the layout change. Stack order: **this PR → #35247 → #35245 → #34613**.

## Motivation

The unified memory pool stores MHA and SWA KV in a page-major envelope whose per-layer slices 
are strided. Every attention backend therefore has to reconstruct a 4-D view of that envelope, and 
in practice only Triton does — which is why the unified pool is Triton-only for these model families 
today. The MLA sub-pool already stores dense per-layer views; this brings MHA and SWA to the 
same layout, so every layer's K and V read through one contiguous tensor addressed by one shared 
block table. That is the precondition for any other backend to read the pool at all.

The correctness fixes that used to lead this branch are gone from it: the SWA tombstone fix was
superseded upstream by #35773 (same bug, fixed via `clear_full_to_swa_mapping`), and the two
Triton translate fixes were speculative-decoding-only in effect and moved out of this series
entirely (the series carries zero `speculative/` changes; spec × unified work follows separately).

## Modifications

Makes the unified pool's MHA and SWA sub-pools expose dense per-layer views, matching the
layout the MLA sub-pool already uses, and moves the ids, the sizing and the pool doors onto that
layout together — the switch is atomic, because an intermediate state would write one id space 
into the other's rows. The view tail-pad is derived from the sub-pool specs rather than passed in,
so no construction site can under-allocate it. Because a dense block array only exists when K and
V rows are equally wide, asymmetric-K/V MHA models are now rejected at startup with a message
naming the four head dims, instead of failing later inside pool construction; MLA is unaffected.

> **Note:** revalidated on the restructured series, rebased onto current main. Accuracy is GSM8K at n=200 per cell over the full cache x sched x cg x page-size grid (60 unified-vs-baseline pairs, 68/68 cells clean); speed is the product-config serving matrix (12 pairs, 5/5 cells clean).

title: refactor(unified-memory): translate the KV write location once, at ForwardBatch construction (#35245)
body:
> **Note on scope — this PR was split out.** It was previously part of #34602 alongside the 
> dense per-layer view feature. Separating them lets the layout change and this refactor be 
> reviewed on their own terms. The stack was also reordered per review: this PR now sits ON 
> the read-path choke point (#35247) and keeps its state there, so nothing is stored on the 
> ForwardBatch. Stack order: **#34602 → #35247 → this PR → #34613**.
>
> Only the last 4 commits are for this PR. The other commits are from the stacked PRs.

## Motivation

Under the unified memory pool a KV location has two forms: the virtual id that ScheduleBatch-side
machinery (radix cache, accept bookkeeping, in-flight tracking) reads, and the kernel-facing id the 
store kernels need. Today each attention backend and each pool door performs that translation 
itself. The same location is translated a different number of times depending on which path a forward 
takes, and every new consumer has to remember to translate — a silent-corruption failure mode, 
since writing a virtual id as though it were physical lands KV in the wrong slot rather than raising.

## Modifications

Establishes a single rule for the write path: ScheduleBatch-side tensors stay virtual always, and 
each ForwardBatch is translated exactly once, at its construction. Every downstream consumer 
— backend metadata, cuda-graph refill, the write door — becomes a passthrough, and the 
backends' own write-side translations are removed. The rebind produces a fresh tensor rather 
than mutating in place, because the scheduler-side machinery reads the same tensors and 
requires virtual ids; for hybrid-SWA models the two rails are derived in the one order that is 
correct, since a single virtual id maps to two different kernel-facing ids.

The translation results live on the per-runner `KVIndexTranslator` (the pool subsystem), not on the 
ForwardBatch — with more hybrid attention kinds a forward carries more kernel-facing id spaces, 
and one ForwardBatch field per id space does not scale. Backends fetch the swa-side rail into 
their own attention metadata through `resolve_swa_write_loc`, which recognizes the prepared 
loc or any torch view of it by address-range containment. That is what removes every piece of 
carry code: TBO child slices and cuda-graph replay views resolve as-is (this PR touches neither 
`two_batch_overlap.py` nor the graph runners), and the two transforms that genuinely replace 
the tensor — the eager input registry's static-buffer rebuild and DP-sync padding — hand the 
new tensor over explicitly.

title: feat(unified-memory): read unified pool from attention backends fa3/flashinfer/trtllm_mha/flashmla (#34613)
body:
> **Note on scope — this PR was split.** It previously contained both the read-path refactor 
> and this backend migration. The refactor is now a separate PR that this one stacks on, so 
> the mechanism can be reviewed independently of the per-backend work. 
> Stack order: **#34602 → #35245 → #35247 → this PR**.
>
> Only the last 8 commits are for this PR. The other commits are from the stacked PRs.

## Motivation

With the read path behind a single choke point, the remaining attention backends can read 
the unified memory pool without carrying any id-space logic of their own. This PR does that 
migration and widens the server's allow-list accordingly, which is what lifts the unified pool 
from Triton-only to the backends users actually run.

## Modifications

Migrates FlashAttention (fa3/fa4), FlashInfer's MHA and MLA backends, trtllm_mla together
with the two backends that subclass it, and trtllm_mha onto the choke point's canonical page
tables. Each backend keeps its existing builder for non-unified pools and dispatches to the 
shared one only when the source is active, so the change is inert off the unified path. The MLA 
model doors' read indices are translated at their production sites (the deepseek MHA mixin), 
which lets both pool doors become passthrough and deletes the last pool-resident translate 
hook. The now-unused backend hook shim is deleted and replaced by an enforcement scan, so 
the boundary cannot be re-crossed silently. The startup allow-list is widened to match what the backends 
can now serve — fa3/fa4/FlashInfer/trtllm_mha for the MHA and SWA families, plus flashmla 
for MLA — and end-to-end cells pin the resulting matrix.

| model class | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| unified MHA/SWA (uniform rows) | `triton` | `triton, fa3, fa4, flashinfer, trtllm_mha` |
| unified MLA | `triton, fa3, trtllm_mla, flashinfer, cutedsl_mla, tokenspeed_mla` | + `flashmla` |
| asymmetric K/V, or env-forced strided | `triton` | `triton` (unchanged) |

`unified_mem_hooks.py` is deleted. After the fold, two translate residents remain
outside the choke point, each by design and neither reachable from a backend: the
allocator-internal v2p implementations (the mechanism the choke point calls) and
the PD transfer-plane `translate_kv_indices_for_transfer` (RDMA staging, outside
the forward path). **A registered source scan enforces this** — it fails if any
file under `layers/attention/` calls a unified translate, probes for one, or
imports the deleted hooks module.

title: [DCP] Support decode context parallelism on the trtllm_mla decode path (#33926)
body:
## Motivation

Draft for the unassigned `trtllm_mla` decode path item in the DCP roadmap #29736 (also relevant to #26432).

`trtllm_mla` has no DCP decode path. `forward_decode` builds its page table and `seq_lens` from the global sequence lengths and returns a bare tensor, while under DCP the model routes decode through `attn_mqa_for_dcp_decode` and expects a rank-local `(out, lse)` pair. The DCP code already in `trtllm_mla_backend.py` covers only speculative `target_verify`, and delegates to `_run_decode_kernel`, which the base rejected — only the `cutedsl_mla` / `tokenspeed_mla` subclasses served it.

This is reachable without asking for it: `arg_groups/overrides.py` auto-selects `trtllm_mla` on sm100 for `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, and `forward_mla.py` routes decode to `attn_mqa_for_dcp_decode` whenever `get_parallel().dcp_enabled` is set, regardless of backend.

### The approach, and its main assumption

flashinfer implements in-kernel DCP only for the CuTeDSL MLA kernel and rejects it elsewhere (`_validate_mla_dcp_args` in `flashinfer/mla/_core.py`), so spec-decode × DCP on `trtllm_mla` is blocked upstream and stays rejected here.

The assumption this draft rests on is that a `q_len == 1` decode does not need it: `cp_world` / `cp_rank` / `causal_seqlens_kv_global` exist so a kernel can resolve a per-query global causal bound, and that bound only varies across query rows when `q_len > 1`. With a single query token the cyclic owner rule should already select exactly the causally visible prefix, leaving the rank-local page table and `seq_lens` sufficient. `trtllm-gen` already supports `return_lse`.

## Modifications

- **Hoist the DCP metadata plumbing onto `TRTLLMMLABackend`.** The rank-local length and page-table helpers were duplicated between `cutedsl_mla_backend.py` and `tokenspeed_mla_backend.py`; both carried a TODO to collapse them into the base. They are kernel-agnostic, so the base now owns them and both subclasses define only their kernel call and decode forward. Every branch is a no-op when DCP is off.
- **`_run_decode_kernel`**: forwards `return_lse`, and narrows the blanket `cp_world > 1 or return_lse` refusal to `cp_world > 1 and causal_seqs is not None` — callers needing a global causal bound signal it by passing `causal_seqs`.
- **`forward_decode`**: new `_forward_decode_dcp` returns the rank-local `(out, lse)`, with `fixup_zero_kv_rows` neutralizing ranks owning no slice of a request.
- **LSE base**: resolved per backend in `__init__` from a `backend -> bool` mapping rather than a class attribute. `TRTLLMMLABackend` t …[truncated]

title: fix(unified-memory): forward the KV-index translator through every wrapper backend (#37307)
body:
## Motivation

`AttentionBackend.kv_index_translator` is a class attribute that defaults to
`None`. A backend that **wraps** another and does not re-expose the inner
backend's copy therefore answers "this backend needs no translation".

Every producer that reaches the translator through the *live backend* rather
than through a runner then skips translation silently. The MLA
chunked-prefix-cache path is one:
`ForwardBatchDeepseekMHAMixin.prepare_chunked_kv_indices` reads
`get_attn_backend().kv_index_translator` and translates only
`if src is not None`, so it hands the kernel raw **virtual** ids for the shared prefix.
Nothing raises — virtual and physical ids share a value range, so the gather
simply reads the wrong rows.

Hybrid models (mamba/GDN + full attention) serve every forward through
`HybridLinearAttnBackend`, which forwards the pool and `req_to_token` but not
the translator. Three other wrappers have the same omission.

The damage needs all three of: `--enable-unified-memory` (translation actually
required), an MLA backend (only fa3 / flashinfer / flashmla take the
chunked-prefix path; Triton does not), and a radix cache (only then is there a
shared prefix to read back). On Kimi-Linear-48B that is **gsm8k 0.89–0.92 →
0.05–0.31 on six of six such cells**, while the same configuration on Triton,
and every chunked-prefill cell, stays correct.

## Modifications

**Four wrappers need the forward, not one.** They spell the wrapped field
`full_attn_backend`, `prefill_backend`/`decode_backend`, `backend`/`swa_backend`
and `dense`, so nothing keyed on the attribute name finds them all:

* `layers/attention/hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py` — from the full-attention
  backend, beside the pool and `req_to_token` it already forwards.
* `layers/attention/hybrid_attn_backend.py` — from the model runner, which is
  where it already takes the pool.
* `layers/attention/dots_hybrid_backend.py` — twice: the DSA wrapper from its
  inner backend, the SWA/MLA wrapper from its swa backend.
* `layers/attention/minimax_sparse_backend.py` — the hybrid wrapper, from its
  dense backend.

`mem_cache/kv_index_translator.py` — `assert_backends_carry_translator`, which
refuses at boot when a reachable backend carries someone else's translator or
none at all, and is inert on a pool that needs no translation.

`model_executor/model_runner.py` — run that guard over the built backends, right
after they are constructed. Adding a forward is easy to forget in a *new*
wrapper and the failure is silent by construction, so the runtime check is what
makes it loud.

title: [AMD] Enable 12-head MLA aiter fp8 Gluon decode (batched bh16bn128). (#34647)
body: Enable 12-head MLA aiter fp8 Gluon decode on gfx950 for Kimi-K3 TP8 (12 local heads). If aiter is not updated to the target version, fall back to use the existing zero-pad + mla_decode_fwd. No behavior change on older containers until aiter/Triton are upgraded. below is the dependency: **aiter runtime dependencies** (container/image, not pinned in this repo): - [ROCm/aiter#4480](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4480) (**merged** to `main`, [`fb82bf7`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/fb82bf7e20adaa9918c9d4bc80e4ff91f000823e)): fp8 Gluon `bh16bn128`, batch>1. - [ROCm/aiter#4555](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4555) (on `main`): decode CUDA graph KV-split budget. - Triton >= 3.7: Gluon `cga_layout` on gfx950. ## Motivation Kimi-K3 at TP8 exposes 12 MLA heads/GPU. The fast aiter persist decode ASM wants head counts divisible by 16 and has no native fp8 12-head path, so fp8 serving had to zero-pad to 16 and go through slower kernels — especially painful at long context under decode CUDA graph. aiter already has a Gluon kernel with a native 12-head masked MFMA tile and an fp8 KV regime (bh16bn128). title: [Feature] Unified memory: support decode context parallelism for Kimi-Linear (#36890)
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-unified-memory` asserted `dcp_size == 1`, so the unified memory pool
and decode context parallelism could not be used together. This enables the
combination for Kimi-Linear (MLA hybrid Mamba).

The two features each rewrite the KV location space, and they had never been
composed:

- DCP hands out a **widened** virtual id space — `dcp_size` logical ids share
  one stored row, and a rank owns the ids with `loc % dcp_size == dcp_rank`.
- The unified pool adds its own transform on top, virtual -> physical -> dense
  (`translate_kv_loc_dense`, the page-major envelope's dense per-layer views).

## Modifications

The composition rule is that **every DCP index kernel already collapses
`loc // dcp_size` when it builds an index** (`create_triton_kv_indices_for_dcp_triton`,
`update_kv_lens_and_indices`, `filter_dcp_local_kv_indices`, and the
`dcp_local_prefix_kv_indices` slice). So `translate_kv_loc*` keeps speaking the
collapsed id space, and only the allocation surface widens.

**Allocator (`multi_ended_allocator.py`).** `MultiEndedAllocator` splits its
page size in two: `page_size` stays the VIRTUAL one (`ps * dcp_size`) that the
scheduler and tree cache read — matching `PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator`'s
existing DCP contract — and a new `pool_page_size` is the PHYSICAL rows one page
occupies. Page ids are invariant under the widening, so `virtual_to_physical` /
`physical_to_virtual`, compaction and the byte budget are all unchanged;
capacity scales by `dcp_size` over the same rows. Both are equal when
`dcp_size == 1`, so the non-DCP path is byte-for-byte unaffected.

**Write path.** `out_cache_loc` is the one location that reaches the pool still
widened, so the write side gets its own hook, `translate_write_loc_dense` /
`HybridLinearKVPool._full_write_translate`, split from the read-side
`_full_translate`. It resolves ownership, collapses, and translates, sending the
rows this rank does not own to dense id 0 — the reserved padding sink the MLA
write kernels already skip. `UnifiedMLATokenToKVPool` then writes with
`dcp_resolved=True` so `set_mla_kv_buffer_triton` does not apply the owner rule
a second time.

**flashinfer-MLA.** Decode ran the unified translate *before* the DCP shard;
that order is swapped, and `plan_dcp_decode_metadata` now returns the compacted
shard length so only that prefix is translated. Its paged prefill reads the
all-gathered `dcp_kv_buffer` and has `attn_dcp_metadata.dcp_kv_indices`
overwrite `kv_indices`, so the translate there is skipped entirely rather than
reordered — on widened ids `virt // page_size` walked of …[truncated]

body:
**Motivation:** a 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) box can hold DeepSeek-V4-Flash, but on
current main the only configuration that starts there is the slow torch fallback — this PR
makes the DeepGEMM and FlashInfer paths work on SM120, cutting decode latency up to 3.4x.

It routes the sparse-MLA indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits kernel, enables batched
sparse-MLA prefill through FlashInfer, and unblocks the DeepGEMM FP4 MoE backend.

## Split out of this PR

Following @Fridge003's review, the changes here that were not SM120 enablement now have
their own PRs:

- #35116 — allocate the page-split buffer outside inference mode (correctness fix)
- #35118 — fuse the hc-prenorm combine into a Triton kernel (arch-independent)

**This PR now depends on #35116**: without it the page-split buffer is allocated under
inference mode during autotune and CUDA graph capture cannot write to it. Will rebase once
it lands.

The E2E tables below were measured with #35118 still in this tree. Measured separately on
the same box with only that kernel toggled (ISL 8K, BS1, TP4, deep_gemm MoE), it accounts
for **3.2% of the TPOT gain** (12.81 -> 12.40 ms, two repeats each, run-to-run spread
0.01 ms) and roughly 2% of TTFT. Discount the tables by that much, or land #35118 first to
reproduce them as written.

## What is in it

1. **Sparse-MLA indexer on DeepGEMM** — route the indexer to DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits
   kernel instead of the eager-torch fallback that scales with batch x context and dominates
   decode. Opt in with `SGLANG_FP8_PAGED_MQA_LOGITS_TORCH=0 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_INDEXER=0`.
2. **Batched sparse-MLA prefill** — prefill (q_len > 64) goes through FlashInfer's
   `_sparse_mla_sm120_paged_attention`; indexer metadata is chunked at M=4096 (the DeepGEMM
   row cap is SKU-dependent) and built once per batch instead of per layer.

5. **SM120 kernel fixes** — u64 page-split copy, sparse-prefill head pad removal, TileLang
   `mhc_pre` compile fix, and the paged-MQA metadata kernel now sizes its shared-memory

title: Build the unified read stream directly, without the page-table rectangle (#37512)
body:
> **Stack** — second of four. **Depends on #37511** (its base branch); review only the commits above `Test the fused tombstone by what it must do`. #37550 → #37560 sit on top.

## Motivation

Three of the seven backends that read the unified pool never wanted a page table. They built a `[max_bs, max_pages]` rectangle and handed it straight to `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton` to repack into the indptr-addressed stream a paged wrapper plans over; no attention kernel ever read the rectangle.

A rectangle's width is bounded by `max_context_len`, because any single request could be that long and every row must be as wide as the widest. At ps=1, max_bs 256 and a 1M context that reserves 268M slots against a pool that holds 8.15M tokens — 32x more than any reachable state. The stream holds one id per resident token, so its length is `sum(seq_lens)`, which the pool bounds exactly.

## Modifications

One gather-and-translate, two delivery forms:

```
PAGE TABLE    out[b, c] = entry(b, c)                              rows a uniform stride apart
TOKEN STREAM  out[row_starts[b] + p] = entry(b, p//ps)*ps + p%ps   indptr-addressed
```

The rule that comes out of it is stateable: **a consumer that plans over a stream calls `fill_packed_read_stream` (flashinfer_mla, flashinfer, triton); a consumer whose kernel reads a page table fills the table it already owns, via `fill_read_table` (flashattention, trtllm_mha, trtllm_mla, flashmla).**

- The two forms share one `@triton.jit`, differing by two constexpr: `row_starts` null means a uniform stride, and `EMIT_PER_TOKEN` selects page or token granularity. The CPU reference paths share `_entries` for the same reason.
- flashinfer_mla, flashinfer and triton fill the stream directly. `kv_view` was threaded through five frames of each flashinfer updater chain; the decode chains never needed the real pool indices (a rectangle is indexed by batch lane, so its row ids were `arange(bs)`) and now take them instead.
- The second half of the rule was already half-true: trtllm_mla and flashmla pass their own block table and consume it in place. flashattention and trtllm_mha each held a *second* rectangle — trtllm_mha's own `page_table` is explicitly not written under unified (`skip_page_table=unified`) while `kv_read_tables` is what gets bound, so one of its two identically-shaped buffers was dead. Both now match their siblings, and **`make_capture_tables` is deleted.**

title: [Feature] Unified memory: support decode context parallelism for the trtllm_mla family (#37693)
body:
## Motivation

#36890 added decode context parallelism to the unified memory pool, but gated `--enable-unified-memory --dcp-size > 1` to `--attention-backend flashinfer`. That excludes `cutedsl_mla`, which is the DCP-native MLA decode kernel on Blackwell (flashinfer accepts `enable_dcp=True` for no other backend) and what the B300 hosts run. So the feature was unusable there.

The reason for the gate is that unified memory plus DCP has two read-index production routes, and #36890 converted only one:

1. **flashinfer** — `plan_dcp_decode_metadata` compacts this rank's widened ids in place, then the caller converts them with `KVIndexTranslator.translate_dcp_read_ids`.
2. **the `trtllm_mla` family** (`trtllm_mla`, `cutedsl_mla`, `tokenspeed_mla`) — a block table built by `create_mla_kv_page_table_for_dcp`, which gathers a rank's cyclic slice straight out of `req_to_token`, bypassing `build_index_table` entirely.

Route 2 collapsed the widened virtual id (`// dcp_size`) and stopped there. That is correct on a static pool, where the collapsed page *is* the physical page, but under the unified pool it is still virtual and needs one more hop through the pool's page table.

## Modifications

- `create_mla_kv_page_table_for_dcp` takes the pool's virtual-to-physical page table (`HAS_V2P`) and scales the physical page by `kernel_page_multiplier` — the same conversion `build_kv_read_table` already performs for the non-DCP block-table backends. A `-1` in `req_to_token` and a freed v2p row both clamp to entry 0, the reserved padding page.
- `KVIndexTranslator` exposes `full_v2p_table` / `full_page_multiplier`, for the one class of producer `build_index_table` cannot serve.
- `_validate_unified_memory_dcp` admits the `trtllm_mla` family. `flashmla` and `cutlass_mla` stay out: neither has a DCP-local page-table builder to extend.

Two write-path defects the same configuration exposes, both fixed here:

- The `cutedsl_mla` / `tokenspeed_mla` DCP decode wrote KV at `forward_batch.out_cache_loc`. A captured decode on the unified pool must not: `rebind_write_loc` returns a *fresh* tensor, so the graph replays against a buffer it never recorded. Both now use the base class's capture-stable `_decode_kernel_loc`, as the non-DCP `trtllm_mla` decode already did.
- The fused fp8 KV scatter passed `dcp_world_size=attn_dcp_size` unconditionally. The unified pool declares `write_loc_is_dcp_resolved`, so its loc arrives already collapsed with non-owned rows sent to the padding sink; applying the owner rule a second time divides a kernel-facing id.

title: [AMD] Fix DSV4 unified attention sink TP slice (#35092)
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 stores `attn_sink` as a global per-head parameter. The non-unified path slices it by attention-TP rank, but the unified-KV branch passed the global tensor directly. Unified prefill truncated it to the first `H` entries and unified decode indexed from head zero, so every nonzero attention-TP rank consumed rank 0's sink values.

This affects pure TP configurations such as TP8/DP1. Baseline/candidate token comparisons cannot detect it when both arms share the same routing bug.

## Modifications

- Pass the existing TP-local sink slice to the unified backend.
- Strip the FlashMLA-only zero padding so the unified backend receives exactly `[n_local_heads]` values.
- Add a real `MQALayer.forward` regression for TP8 ranks 0, 3, and 7 with distinct per-head sink values.

## Accuracy Tests

The bug predates this PR: `attn_sink=self.attn_sink` entered upstream main with unified-KV support in `f2bcdb050` (#27380). It is present in this PR's base (`92b1d382c`) and was still present in upstream main `4b06f917c` when rechecked.

- Production Triton decode vs the same reference: max abs `0.001953125`, mean abs `6.20e-05`, passed `atol=rtol=0.02`.

title: [AMD][DSv4] Switch output projection gemm (oproj_a) to fp8 (#37423)
body: ## Motivation On DeepSeek-V4, the MLA output projection is split into two GEMMs: `wo_a` absorbs the attention output into the low-rank o space, and `wo_b` projects back to the hidden size. On ROCm, `wo_a` runs in **bf16** today while `wo_b` already runs in fp8 block-scale — so the absorb GEMM reads full-precision weights on a decode step that is bound by weight traffic. sglang already has an fp8 `wo_a` path behind `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM` (on by default), but it is built on DeepGEMM's `fp8_einsum`, which is CUDA-only. `model_hook.py` therefore force-disables the flag on every HIP device, and ROCm silently falls back to the bf16 batched GEMM. title: [AMD] Optimize Kimi-K3 Triton MLA prefill on gfx950 (#35770)
body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3 uses two attention representations during prefill at TP8 on MI355X:

- Fresh/zero-prefix MHA: 12 heads with QK/V dimensions 192/128.
- Cached-prefix absorbed MLA: 12 query heads, one KV head, and QK/V
  dimensions 576/512.

Current Triton prefill leaves performance on the table for both shapes:

1. The exact K3 kernels use one pipeline stage and natural-exponential
   online softmax.
2. Absorbed 576/512 prefill processes one full 512-wide value accumulator,
   increasing register pressure.
3. FP8 cached-prefix P·V can underflow small softmax probabilities.
4. Aiter supports native FP8 zero-prefix prefill, but Triton lacks an
   equivalent opt-in path.

## Changes

### K3 prefill tuning

- Use two pipeline stages for exact gfx950 K3 192/128 and N32 576/512
  prefill kernels.
- Fold `log2(e)` into the attention scale and use `exp2` for unmodified K3
  logits.
- Convert stored LSE back to natural-log units.
- Preserve current compact ragged-grid scheduling and the generic
  Triton-3.7 fallback.

### 4×128 absorbed MLA kernel

Add a dedicated split-dimension kernel for cached-prefix K3 MLA:

```text
Q/K latent: 4 × 128
Q/K tail:       64
V/output:   4 × 128
```

The kernel maintains one online-softmax state and four independent FP32
value accumulators before concatenating the normalized 128-wide outputs.

Dispatch is restricted to:

- gfx950;
- 12 query heads and one KV head;
- QK/V dimensions 576/512;
- BF16 current Q/K/V and output;
- BF16 cached prefix with unit scales, or opt-in FP8 cached prefix with
  supported descales;
- causal attention;
- page size 1;
- contiguous last dimensions;
- no custom mask, sliding window, logit cap, XAI temperature, sink, LSE,
  score modifier, auxiliary tensor, or skipped stage.

Unsupported calls immediately use the existing generic kernel.

### FP8 prefill

Add:

```bash
SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=1
```

This is enabled by default. Set `SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0` to disable
native FP8 prefill.

On exact K3 gfx950 shapes:

- Zero-prefix 192/128 Q/K/V are cast from BF16 to FP8 before launch,
  matching Aiter behavior.
- Absorbed 576/512 prefill keeps current-chunk Q/K/V in BF16 while using
  the FP8 cached prefix.
- Softmax probabilities are multiplied by `FP8_MAX` before FP8 P·V and
  the accumulator contribution is divided by the same factor.
- Non-unit cached-prefix K/V descales are supported.

The default-on path achieved 98% GSM8K accuracy in model-level validation.

## Performance

title: [AMD][DSV4] Fix unified-KV pool sizing and SWA ring accounting (#30315)
body:
## Consolidation note

This PR now also contains the SWA per-request ring runtime accounting and tests previously reviewed in #31040. The two pieces must land together: with only the original pool-sizing commits, the DSV4 Flash and Pro MI35x jobs hit GPU memory access faults during concurrent prefill; the runtime ring reconciliation at the combined tip prevents the allocator from issuing locations beyond the fixed per-request SWA ring.

## Motivation

The DSV4 `unified_kv` backend has a different physical KV layout than the fp8 path, but `DSV4PoolConfigurator` sized both identically. Under `unified_kv` this over-allocates memory (and can OOM), because:

- KV is stored in **bf16 over the full latent** (`attn_head_dim * 2` bytes), not the fp8(nope) + bf16(rope) + scale 584-byte cell.
- SWA and the c4/c128 compress-states are **fixed per-request rings** (`num_req_slots * ring_size`), independent of `full_token`, so they must be fixed biases rather than per-token terms.

## Modifications

All changes are gated on the same `is_unified_kv_triton()` / `_unified_kv` switch the pool itself uses, so sizing and allocation cannot drift apart. **No behavior change on the non-unified (fp8) path.**

### Pool sizing (`pool_configurator.py`)

- Use bf16 full-latent bytes for the per-token coeff on the unified path (`_get_bytes_per_full_token`).
- Exclude SWA from the per-token coeff and account for it as a fixed bias (`_fixed_swa_bytes`), inflated for the speculative draft worker the same way as the coeff.
- Move the **c4 compress-state (attn + indexer)** off the per-token coeff and size it as a request-scoped fixed bias (`_fixed_c4_state_bytes` / `_unified_c4_state_pool_size`), finalized once `max_running_requests` is known — mirroring the c128 state pool. title: Support NoPE layers in the tokenspeed_mla FP8 prefill hook (#38152)
body:
## Motivation

Three `extra-b-test-4-gpu-b200` jobs fail on main ([run 33962519343](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33962519343)): `test_kimi_linear_dcp4.py`, `test_kimi_linear_dcp_dspark4.py`, `test_unified_radix_cache_kl_dcp.py`, all Kimi Linear on `tokenspeed_mla` + `fp8_e4m3` under DCP. Every TP rank crashes during prefill and the server is SIGKILLed:

```
File ".../layers/attention/tokenspeed_mla_backend.py", line 265, in prepare_prefill_qkv
    cos_sin_cache=layer.rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache,
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'cos_sin_cache'
```

Surfaced by #35770, which taught `resolve_attn_backend()` to unwrap `HybridLinearAttnBackend.full_attn_backend`. Kimi Linear is hybrid KDA/MLA, so prefill used to resolve to the wrapper, which has no `prepare_prefill_qkv` hook, and took the BF16 path guarded by `if self.rotary_emb is not None`. title: [ROCm] Take the fused DSA metadata kernels and drop redundant work from the absorb path (#37124)
body:
Three ROCm-only changes on the DSA decode path. All numbers are GLM-5.2-MXFP4 /
MI355X / TP4, agentic replay at concurrency 4, paired per request against the
same branch without the change.

## Fused DSA metadata kernels

The five sites that build DSA's per-step metadata read `is_cuda() and not
_is_hip`, so HIP falls back to a PyTorch sequence of seven or eight ops. The
kernels they skip are three `@triton.jit` functions in
`kernels/ops/attention/dsa_metadata.py` — no `tl.dot`, no atomics, no CUDA
intrinsics. Their only device references are `.is_cuda` asserts, which are True
for HIP tensors.

The fallback is worse than its op count suggests. On target-verify it does a
`req_to_token[req_pool_indices, :max_seqlen_k]` gather where `max_seqlen_k` is
the *graph buffer's* width, not the request's kv length. At `context_len`
1048576 that is a `[bs, 1.05M]` int32 gather, a `[bs*6, 1.05M]` transient and a
100 MB copy — every decode step. The Triton kernel writes `page_table_1`
directly and returns early on column blocks past `kv_len`, so at this workload's
median 62k context it touches ~6% of them.

**ITL ratio p50 0.984** over 82 requests, 58 of them faster, sign test
p = 0.0002. TTFT 0.998.

2% is small enough that the direction matters more than the magnitude: 58/82 is
what says it reproduces, and the effect is the size the traffic argument
predicts rather than something larger, because PyTorch's caching allocator
reuses the same 100 MB block every step and only the bandwidth is recovered.

## q_all cat-skip on target-verify

`_fused_rope_cat_and_cache` already returns the concatenated absorbed query, and
decode hands it to `attn_mqa` with `q_rope=None` so the backend reuses it as a
view. Target-verify instead split it back into two views and let
`forward_extend` run `concat_mla_absorb_q_general` over them — rebuilding a
tensor byte-identical to the one it started from, one `CatArrayBatchedCopy` per
layer per step.

`assert q_rope is not None` in `forward_extend` sat directly above an
`if q_rope is not None ... else` whose else branch is exactly the zero-copy path,
so the assert was what made that branch dead code. `forward_decode` already had
the shape this needs — a `q_all=None` sentinel and `if q_all is None or not
_is_hip` at the point of use, the `not _is_hip` clause keeping CUDA
byte-identical. This mirrors it into `forward_extend`.

Real prefill keeps the split form: the Triton sparse-MLA kernel reads `q_nope`
and `q_rope` separately, and its own gate (`q_nope.shape[0] >= 512`) never
matches target-verify  …[truncated]

title: [Perf] Unified memory: close the DCP decode gap on Blackwell (#37926)
body:
## Motivation

Unified memory (`--enable-unified-memory`) under decode context parallelism was
measurably slower than the static pool on Blackwell. The Hopper fix (#37511) did
not carry over: on a B300 with Kimi-Linear at TP2/DCP2 and `cutedsl_mla`, the
unified pool ran **1.96% behind static** (worst config -4.06%).

Profiling showed the gap is entirely CPU-side. GPU kernel time was slightly
*lower* for the unified pool, while it issued ~456 more `cudaLaunchKernel` calls
per profiled window. A Blackwell decode step is short enough that per-step
launch overhead is visible; the same overhead hides inside a Hopper step.

Two structural causes, both fixed here.

**The write-loc translate ran as an eager op chain.** Converting a virtual write
loc to kernel-facing ids is `v2p[t // ps] * ps * mult + t % ps` clamped at 0,
which is ~6 torch ops, and ~12 once the DCP owner rule (`loc % dcp_size ==
dcp_rank`) is resolved on top. It runs per forward, outside any CUDA graph, so
every op is a real launch on the critical path. It is now one Triton kernel.

**The unified pool was excluded from the mamba fused replay state-indices
path.** The gate's stated reason was that its mapping is "not a flat table
gather", which was not true: `UnifiedMambaSlotAllocator.translate` is exactly
`virtual_to_physical[virtual_ids]`. Teaching the fused kernel one optional v2p
gather lets the unified pool take the single-launch path like every other pool.

## Modification

Three commits.

## Motivation


#30339 fixed a stale per-request SWA ring read on radix prefix reuse for DeepSeek-V4 with the unified_kv backend. The mechanism: hold back a trailing sliding window from the radix match so it is re-prefilled into the requesting slot's own ring instead of being inherited from whichever request previously occupied that req_pool_idx.
It shipped as a `SWARadixCache.swa_reprefill_tail_tokens()` override, gated only on the backend:
```
# swa_radix_cache.py, from #30339
if self.sliding_window_size and is_unified_kv_triton():
    return self.sliding_window_size
return 0
```
At the time SWARadixCache was the live path for unified_kv + radix + HiCache off. (The HiCache path had its own override on UnifiedRadixCache, added a day earlier by #29417 and deliberately scoped to HiCache via `cache_controller is not None`.)

However, 4 days after #30339 merged, #30468 (Using UnifiedRadixTree by default for SWA, Mamba, and DSA models, afa3c06d1) then replaced the hybrid-SWA branch in `registry.py`:
```

         if ctx.full_tokens_per_layer == 0:
             return PureSWARadixCache(params=params)
-        from sglang.srt.mem_cache.swa_radix_cache import SWARadixCache
-
-        return SWARadixCache(params=params)
+        return _create_unified_radix_cache(ctx, server_args, params)
```
Two consequences:
1. SWARadixCache is no longer constructed anywhere in-tree. Grepping current main for the symbol returns only type annotations, the type(...) is SWARadixCache checks  in `kv_canary/radix_cache_walker.py`, a docstring in `pure_swa_radix_cache.py`, a comment in `multi_ended_allocator.py`, and a mention in the unified-cache README.

## Motivation

Under MLP sync (DP attention, DeepEP, or `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`) the eager and cuda-graph runners pad the request count to the attn-tp alignment (`get_eager_max_batch_size` / `get_cuda_graph_max_batch_size`), so the warm-up dummy batch and the largest captured decode batch can be wider than `req_to_token_pool.size`.

`FlashInferMLAAttnBackend` sized `kv_indptr`, `qo_indptr` and `q_indptr_decode` to the raw pool size (and the cuda-graph buffers are clones of those), so the server died at startup:

```
File ".../flashinfer_mla_backend.py", line 889, in call_begin_forward
    kv_indptr[1 : bs + 1] = torch.cumsum(paged_kernel_lens, dim=0)
RuntimeError: The expanded size of the tensor (14) must match the existing size (16) at non-singleton dimension 0.  Target sizes: [14].  Tensor sizes: [16]
```

Hit with Kimi-K3 TP8 + `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` on the flashinfer MLA backend (the mamba state cache capped `max_running_requests` to 14, attn_tp=8 padded the batch to 16). Any MLA model on the flashinfer backend with an MLP-sync feature and a request cap that is not a multiple of attn_tp reproduces it, e.g. `--tp 4 --enable-dp-attention --dp 2 --attention-backend flashinfer --max-running-requests 3` (per-rank pool 1, padded batch 2). The non-MLA `flashinfer_backend.py` already sizes these buffers with `get_cuda_graph_max_batch_size`; the MLA backend was the only one left on the raw pool size.

## Modifications

- `flashinfer_mla_backend.py`: size `kv_indptr` / `qo_indptr` / `q_indptr_decode` (and the multi-step draft backend's buffers) to `get_cuda_graph_max_batch_size(req_to_token_pool.size)`, matching the non-MLA flashinfer backend.

# Fast Triton Sparse MLA Kernels for DSA (Prefill + Decode)

## Summary

This adds `triton` as an explicit DSA prefill/decode backend:

```bash
--dsa-prefill-backend triton
--dsa-decode-backend triton
```

The new backend provides pure Triton sparse MLA kernels for the fp8 DSA path on ROCm, validated on MI355X (gfx950) and MI300X (gfx942). It replaces the previous Triton prefill env-var gate, SGLANG_DSA_TRITON_PREFILL, with a faster kernel exposed through the normal backend option and adds a fast Triton kernel for the decode path.

## What Changed

- Adds `triton` to `DSA_CHOICES` for `--dsa-prefill-backend` and `--dsa-decode-backend`.
- Adds startup validation in both server-args paths so Triton DSA is only used with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`.
- Adds standalone Triton prefill and decode dispatch branches in `dsa_backend.py`.

title: [NPU][Hicache] Optimize HiCache L2 IO with Memfabric acc_offload (#38826)
body: ## Motivation On Ascend NPU, the existing HiCache L2 (host DRAM) IO path uses `transfer_kv_dim_exchange` with default host memory allocation. This works functionally but has two issues: 1. **Host memory not AIV-de-referencable**: The default `torch.pin_memory` host buffers are only reachable by the SDMA engine; the fused AIV sparse-copy kernel (`offload.kv_exchange_copy`) from the Memfabric `acc_offload` library can only de-reference host VAs that were mapped into the device VA space via the Memfabric offload entity. 2. **Stream synchronization on H2D upload**: A pageable `.to(device)` on NPU completes with `aclrtStreamSynchronize` that drains everything queued on the current stream, serializing the layer-group pipeline and stalling compute. This PR adds the Memfabric-mapped host DRAM allocation and the AscendC sparse-copy IO path, gated behind a single environment variable `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_MEM_BACKEND=memfabric`. **Depends on #L3PR** (Ascend MemCache L3 storage backend). ## Modifications - **`pool_host/common.py`** (+154): Add Memfabric host memory allocator (`alloc_with_memfabric`), lazy initialization (`ensure_memfabric_capacity`), single-switch detection (`memfabric_host_memory_enabled`, `ascendc_io_enabled`), and sync-free H2D upload helpers (`to_device_no_sync`, `track_pinned_staging`) using pinned memory + `torch.npu.Event`. - **`pool_host/mla.py`** (+266): In `MLATokenToKVPoolHost`, add Memfabric host pool allocation path (sizes the GB-aligned reserve from `--hicache-size`/`--hicache-ratio`), add `_transfer_ascendc_sparse_copy` method that launches the fused `offload.kv_exchange_copy` kernel (builds compact per-component metadata array, converts host pointers to DVAs, uploads indices without stream sync), and wire it into H2D/D2H paths when `ascendc_io_enabled()`. - **`managers/cache_controller.py`** (+17): In `submit_device_to_host`, when `ascendc_io_enabled()`, keep token indices on device and upload via `to_device_no_sync` instead of `.cpu()` sync. - **`hardware_backend/npu/utils.py`** (+7): Extend `set_default_server_args` to also handle `disaggregation_decode_enable_offload_kvcache` config resolution. Single switch: `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_MEM_BACKEND=memfabric` enables both the Memfabric host pool allocation and the AIV sparse-copy IO path simultaneously. ## Accuracy Tests No impact on model outputs — this PR only affects the HiCache L2 IO transfer path (D2H backup and H2D load). The KV data content is identical; only the transfer mechanism changes. ## Speed Tests and Profiling before:

title: [NPU][Hicache] Add Ascend Memcache Hicache L3 storage backend (#38827)
body:
## Motivation

SGLang HiCache uses a tiered KV cache architecture: L1 (device/HBM) → L2 (host memory) → L3 (external storage). On CUDA, storage backends such as Mooncake are already supported as HiCache L3, enabling cross-node prefix cache reuse and increasing the effective KV cache capacity.

On Ascend NPU, however, there was previously no corresponding L3 storage backend. As a result, HiCache on Ascend was limited to device + host tiers and could not offload KV cache pages to distributed storage. [Ascend MemCache](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/memcache), built on top of MemFabric, provides a distributed memory pool for Ascend deployments and is a natural fit for HiCache L3.

This PR integrates Ascend MemCache into HiCache as a new L3 storage backend. With `--hicache-storage-backend npu_memcache`, Ascend users can enable cross-node KV cache sharing and reuse, improving prefix cache hit rates and helping reduce TTFT for long-context and multi-turn workloads.


## Modifications

- Add `NpuMemcacheStore`
  - Implements the `HiCacheStorage` interface on top of `memcache_hybrid.DistributedObjectStore`.
  - Supports zero-copy page I/O APIs, including `batch_get`, `batch_set`, and `batch_exists`.

- Register the new storage backend
  - Register `npu_memcache` in `StorageBackendFactory`.
  - Expose it through the existing `--hicache-storage-backend` server argument.
  - Route `npu_memcache` through the zero-copy I/O path in `cache_controller`, aligned with Mooncake.

- Support cache key layout and parallelism
  - Keep compatibility with MHA / MLA models.
  - Support the `page_first_kv_split` layout.


- Add configuration and debugging support
  - Add `SGLANG_HICACHE_MEMCACHE_CONFIG_PATH` for MemCache configuration.
  - Add trace/debug environment variables for easier diagnosis.
  - Add `start_meta_service.py` to launch the MemCache MetaService.
  - Add a README covering installation, deployment, and quick-start usage.

- Update server argument checks
  - Include `npu_memcache` in storage layout compatibility checks.
  - Align the validation behavior with the existing Mooncake backend.


## Accuracy Tests

title: [Perf] trtllm_mla: reuse the fused fp8 KV/Q prepare on target verify (#39232)
linked_issues: #39107 [Feature] TRTLLM MLA target verification misses fused FP8 KV/Q preparation in forward_extend
body:
## Motivation

Closes #39107.

`TRTLLMMLABackend.forward_decode` already fuses the fp8 no-RoPE preparation (bf16 -> fp8 quantize + KV scatter + `[q_nope | q_rope]` concat) into one `set_mla_kv_concat_q_fp8` launch. Target verify dispatches through `forward_extend`, which on the same inputs still ran the unfused chain unconditionally: `concat_mla_absorb_q` + three aten fp8 casts + the pool's Triton scatter, i.e. five launches per MLA layer instead of one. This is the `cos_sin_cache is None` case, hit by MLA models with no RoPE on the absorbed path (Kimi K3, `skip_rope=True`); RoPE models take the flashinfer `mla_rope_quantize_fp8` path and are unaffected.

Nothing about the fused kernel is decode-specific: it is per-token / per-(token, head), its q/k row strides are runtime parameters, and the capture-stable write loc (`_decode_kernel_loc`) is already filled for `TARGET_VERIFY` under the unified pool. `CuteDslMLABackend` and `TokenspeedMLABackend` inherit `forward_extend`, so their verify takes the same path (including Kimi K3's default DCP config, which routes verify to cutedsl_mla via `speculative_attention_mode="decode"`).

## Modifications

- `forward_extend`, fp8 + `is_target_verify()` + `cos_sin_cache is None`: try the same guarded fused prepare as decode (`save_kv_cache` and `_fused_set_kv_concat_q_fp8` on, `_resolve_fused_write_loc` yields a loc, `covered_fp8` accepts). On success the pool write and the concat are skipped; otherwise the existing `mla_quantize_without_rope_for_fp8` + `set_mla_kv_buffer` chain runs unchanged. No new kernel and no change to the static gate: this is the dispatch fix from the issue, on the existing CUDA JIT kernel.
- New `test/registered/kernel/attention/test_trtllm_mla_fp8_prepare.py`, on the same bare-backend fixture as `TestFusedFp8WriteGate`: `forward_extend` in `TARGET_VERIFY` takes the fused prepare, writes at the capture-stable loc under a translating pool, and keeps the unfused chain with the gate off, pinned to the aten fp8 reference for the pool rows and the query. The pool's writer is a stand-in that refuses on the fused branch and writes on the fallback.

## Accuracy Tests

The fused kernel produces byte-identical rows and query to the aten chain (`test_kimi_k3_prerequisite_ops` already pins that at batch 64); the new test pins the same contract on the verify path. Draft: the GPU tests have not been run locally yet, and a Kimi K3 + trtllm_mla + fp8 KV + MTP accuracy run is still pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Launch count on the verify prepare drops from 5 to 1 per MLA layer. #39107 reports about 1 …[truncated]

title: [AMD][gfx95] Fill the chunked-prefill compute budget exactly (#32888)
body:
## Summary

A prefill batch never reaches `--chunked-prefill-size`: `_update_prefill_budget` charges the page-ceiled extend length against `rem_chunk_tokens` and `rem_input_tokens`, and `add_one_req` floors the last truncation back to a page. On gfx95 that shortfall is expensive — the aiter MLA absorb bmm picks its `EVEN_MN` specialization from a compile-time `constexpr` on `M % BLOCK_SIZE_M`, so a misaligned M runs a different compiled binary, not the same one with a partial tile.

|                        | before             | after              |
| ---------------------- | ------------------ | ------------------ |
| MLA absorb bmm         | 311.2 us @ M=16368 | 155.8 us @ M=16384 |
| instructions           | 3819               | 1562               |
| trace token annotation | `toks=16350`       | `toks=16384`       |

`compute_charge` bills the compute budgets in raw tokens; the KV budgets stay page-ceiled. Below, the ledger spends 16384 while the forward runs 16328 (`page_size=64`, 8100-token prompts) — only whole admissions leak.

| req          | admitted | runs      | charged   | budget left |
| ------------ | -------- | --------: | --------: | ----------: |
| 1            | whole    | 8100      | 8128      | 8256        |
| 2            | whole    | 8100      | 8128      | 128         |
| 3            | chunked  | 128       | 128       | 0           |
| Accu. tokens |          | **16328** | **16384** |             |

## Scope

gfx95 (MI355X) chunked prefill, gated on `SGLANG_EXACT_CHUNK_FILL` **and** `is_gfx95_supported()`. CUDA and other AMD parts keep upstream behaviour on every path, and the dLLM path is excluded. ROCm/aiter#4453 deepens the kernel win but does not gate this PR.

`schedule_policy.py` is common code, so the CUDA no-op is measured rather than asserted. Replaying 48 admission scenarios (`page_size` 1/8/64 × chunk 2048/16384 × four prompt mixes, 114 admissions) against `upstream/main` with the gate off reproduces every budget counter byte-for-byte; forcing it on moves 73 lines, and `page_size=1` is identical either way.

title: [AMD][DSV4] feat: enable fp8 two-pool unified_kv on gfx950 (#37413)
body:
## Motivation


Under `unified_kv`, DSv4 keeps KV in bf16 across the full latent — `qk_nope_head_dim` 448 plus `qk_rope_head_dim` 64, **1024 B per token per layer**. The nope half actually does not need that precision. Storing nope as fp8 with per-tile E8M0 scales while leaving rope in bf16 cuts the row to **640 B** (512 B of fp8 nope at a fixed stride, plus the same 128 B of bf16 rope), which measures out at **1.51× the KV capacity at identical memory** on gfx950. At fixed HBM more tokens stay resident, so longer contexts and higher concurrency fit on the same node.

Off by default behind `SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8`; it requires gfx950 and implies `is_unified_kv_triton()`. Other architectures warn and fall back to bf16, so nothing on the existing path changes.

## Modifications


Two pools instead of one, then every writer and reader of the pool:
- **layout / sizing** — nope is a 512 B fp8 row (448 values + inline e8m0 scales, padded so the stride stays a power of two); rope stays 128 B of bf16. PD disaggregation and HiCache offload are refused for now because both assume one pool per layer.
- **writers** — SWA scatter, fused QK norm+RoPE store, compressor norm+rope store, and the packed ring store used by prefill and target-verify.
- **readers** — decode through aiter's `mla_a8w8` v4 nm asm kernel; prefill through aiter's opus kernel.
- **decode overhead** — drop a `masked_fill_` on empty segments the builders cannot produce, cache `qo_indptr` (it only depends on the token count), skip a `kv.contiguous()` the group-quant kernel does not need (it already takes the row stride), and cap `num_kv_splits` to 4 above 40 tokens where aiter's occupancy heuristic over-splits.

Everything stays behind `SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8` (default off) plus the gfx95 gate. The DSv4 unified_kv path is ROCm-only; the only common-code touch is one new `elif` in the JIT norm+rope-store template, existing branches unchanged.

## What this buys: KV capacity

Four configurations, each a pair of servers with byte-identical CLI differing only in the env switch. Taken on this rebase (`ec07b65ed6 `):

| config | `available_bytes` | bf16 `full_token` | fp8 `full_token` | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | 135.59 GB | 16,126,208 | 24,223,744 | **1.5021×** |
| TP8 + MTP | 132.97 GB | 15,417,344 | 23,161,088 | **1.5023×** |
| TP8 + DP8 | 119.85 GB | 14,399,488 | 21,605,120 | **1.5004×** |
| TP8 + DP8 + MTP | 115.35 GB | 13,612,288 | 20,424,448 | **1.5004×** |
